text_blocks.snippet: Several herbal teas can help soothe acid reflux and heartburn symptoms. Chamomile tea, ginger tea, and licorice tea are popular choices due to their anti-inflammatory and soothing properties. Marshmallow root tea is also known for coating the stomach and easing irritation. Additionally, some blends like NutraReflux include ingredients like slippery elm and fennel to aid digestion and settle the stomach.
snippet_highlighted_words: Chamomile tea, ginger tea, and licorice tea

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at some options:

1. Chamomile Tea: Known for its calming and anti-inflammatory effects, chamomile tea can help reduce acid reflux and promote better sleep, which can be helpful for managing symptoms. 2. Ginger Tea: Ginger is a well-known remedy for digestive issues, including acid reflux. It can help reduce pressure on the lower esophageal sphincter (LES), potentially preventing stomach acid from flowing back up into the esophagus. 3. Licorice Tea: Licorice has anti-inflammatory properties and may help soothe the stomach and esophagus, potentially reducing the severity of acid reflux symptoms. 4. Marshmallow Root Tea: Marshmallow root contains mucilage, a substance that can form a protective layer in the stomach and esophagus, easing irritation caused by stomach acid. 5. Herbal Blends: Some teas combine multiple ingredients to target acid reflux. For example, NutraReflux includes peppermint, licorice, chamomile, Shatavari root, ginger, fennel, slippery elm, and fenugreek. 6. Other Options: Other teas like fennel tea and turmeric tea may also be helpful for some individuals.

list.title: Avoid Mint:
list.snippet: While some herbal teas are helpful, those containing mint or peppermint may trigger acid reflux in some people.

list.title: Consult a Doctor:
list.snippet: If you experience frequent or severe acid reflux, it's important to consult with a healthcare professional for proper diagnosis and treatment.

list.title: Consistency is Key:
list.snippet: For best results, consider drinking these teas regularly, especially after meals or before bedtime.

list.title: Other Lifestyle Factors:
list.snippet: Remember that diet and other lifestyle choices also play a significant role in managing acid reflux. Avoiding trigger foods, eating smaller meals, and staying hydrated can also help, according to GATGI.
